meta.title: Məskən — where to live in Azerbaijan
meta.description: Prices, services, transport, roads and nature for every district of Azerbaijan and every Baku neighbourhood, with AI analysis and a personal fit map.

common.tagline: where to live — by the numbers
common.footer: Data: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), State Statistics Committee of Azerbaijan, Open-Meteo. Some prices are demo values — <link>see sources</link>. Məskən does not give legal or financial advice.

advisor.formula: Calculated by code, not by the AI: data coverage 40% + request completeness 25% + gap between #1 and #2 20% + constraints met 15%.
advisor.footer: Code does the ranking; the AI only explains, using only these areas' numbers. Prices are district averages, not neighbourhood prices. No data is taken from listing sites — the links only open a search.

landing.h1: Where should you live? Answered with data, for you.
landing.lead: We help people buying a home or opening a business choose an area. Describe what you need in one sentence and we show the places that meet your conditions — from {regions} districts, {hoods} city neighbourhoods and {villages} villages and towns — and explain their prices and risks.
landing.q1d: Listing sites show flats, not neighbourhoods. We measure the distance to the metro, schools and kindergartens, plus services and air quality, for every neighbourhood.
landing.q2d: The price per m² varies 2.8-fold between Baku districts. Using listing medians and ten years of commuting costs, we show what a “cheap but far away” home really costs.
landing.q3d: “Kupça hazırlanır” (title extract in preparation), “müqavilə ilə” (by private contract), “etibarnamə ilə” (under power of attorney) — paste the listing and we flag the risks and the documents to check.
landing.f1: rise in new-build prices (Q2 2026, year on year)
landing.f1s: Central Bank review via JAM News, 31 Aug 2026
landing.f2: rise in wages — house prices are growing faster than pay
landing.f3: gap in price per m² between Baku districts (Səbail {a}, Pirallahı {b})
landing.f4: of Baku listings say “çıxarış yoxdur” (no title extract) — out of {n}
landing.s1d: “A flat near the metro in Nərimanov, budget 180k” — the AI turns your request into a goal, budget, location and conditions.
landing.s2d: Code selects and ranks the matching neighbourhoods out of {hoods} — walking distance to the metro, schools, price.
landing.s3d: The AI explains each recommendation with numbers and names its weak spot; the confidence score is calculated from data quality.

sources.metaDesc: Where every figure in Məskən comes from, how it is calculated and where the data is weak.
sources.intro: Every figure in Məskən carries a source badge. This page lists those sources, the calculation rules and where the data is weak. Data updated: {date}.
sources.pricesH: Prices: which are real and which are demo
sources.pricesBody: Azerbaijan has no open, official housing price statistics by district. We took only published figures (listing sites are not scraped): {real} values in total. The remaining {demo} cells are demo values: aligned with the real figures (centre > outskirts, new > old, regions '<' Baku), but they are not market prices and carry a “Demo” badge on the map. Values come from data/manual/prices.csv and can be replaced with a real source without changing any code.

sources.cost: Cost: one AI call uses on average ~2,000 input + ~400 output tokens (measured). A session (~4 calls) costs ≈ $0.006 with gemini-3.7-flash, or ≈ $0.03 at a cautious price; 1,000 users ≈ $6–26. The free Gemini tier is enough for the demo, the cache makes repeat questions free and hosting is free (static data). Details: <link>Quality and tests</link>. Next steps: a 4-week pilot with an estate agent, a price data partnership, monthly OSM refresh.

m.mahalle: Neighbourhoods. 905 neighbourhoods (məhəllə) across Baku, Sumqayıt and Gəncə: the 67 with a boundary in OSM (microdistricts, settlements) are used as they are; the rest of the area is filled with Voronoi cells built from OSM settlement points and metro stations and clipped to district boundaries, so boundaries are approximate (not aligned to streets). Indicators are aggregated from an internal H3 grid (3,700 cells): counts are summed, distances are area-weighted averages and prices are medians; distances to the nearest metro (checked against the 27 operating stations), stop, school, kindergarten and park; names come from OSM settlements. The price is the median if a neighbourhood has ≥5 listings, otherwise the district average.
m.engine: Decision engine. The AI structures the query and explains the result; code filters and ranks matching areas and computes the confidence score (coverage 40%, query completeness 25%, gap between 1st and 2nd 20%, match with constraints 15%).
m.areas: Areas. OSM administrative boundaries: 75 districts/cities and Baku's 12 districts. Sea areas are clipped by the Caspian coastline (islands kept). Population and density: SSC, 01.01.2026.
m.services: Services. OSM features (pharmacies, groceries, schools, kindergartens, hospitals, clinics, banks, cafés, sport, parks etc.) are counted if they fall inside the polygon and divided per 10,000 residents.
m.transport: Transport. Metro and railway stations (unique by name), bus stops, bus/minibus routes mapped in OSM; for Baku districts, the straight-line distance from the centre to the nearest metro.
m.roads: Roads. Main roads, streets and rural tracks; surface from the OSM “surface” tag: asphalt/concrete, dirt/gravel or unknown. On the map, “paved %” is calculated among roads with a known surface.
m.nature: Nature. Land cover is sampled from OSM polygons on a 30×30–36×36 point grid in each area (approximate). Elevation: Open-Meteo, 5×5 grid; terrain: plain (mean '<'200 m, std '<'50), mountain (mean >1000 m or std >250), otherwise foothills. Climate: ERA5 (2025); PM2.5: CAMS model.
m.indices: Indices (0–100). Each indicator is converted to a percentile among areas at the same level, and the index is their average: comfort, transport, education, healthcare, nature, road infrastructure, affordability (inverse of price).
m.fit: Fit. The AI extracts weights from the persona sentence; score = Σ(weight × index) / Σ weight. If the home exceeds the budget, the score is multiplied by 0.3 and marked “over budget”.
m.trueCost: True cost (10 years). Home price + 120 months × (monthly travel cost + hours travelling × value of an hour). Distance = straight line × 1.4; speeds: metro 30, bus 15, car 25 (Baku) / 60 km/h. Approximate model.

ai.1: The AI runs on Google Gemini (flash). The model sees only the area's JSON indicators and may use only the numbers in it; every answer is validated against a JSON schema (zod).
ai.2: Area profiles are generated in advance and cached; persona, Q&A, comparison and legal check are called live and the result is cached.
ai.3: When the AI is unavailable (rate limit, network), the site falls back to a rule-based answer and says so in the text.
ai.4: In the legal check, known risk phrases (“çıxarışsız”, without a title extract; “kupçasız”, without a deed; “etibarnamə ilə”, sold under power of attorney, etc.) are also detected by a deterministic rule, so the AI cannot miss them. A law article is cited only if its text is in our database.

l.1: Prices: bina.az listing medians in 17 areas (2024, a user-supplied dataset; we do not scrape and store aggregates only), 7 published figures, the rest demo. Most districts have no price.
l.2: OSM is incomplete in the regions: few features means “not mapped”, not “not there”. The coverage level is shown for every area.
l.3: Route counts reflect only lines mapped in OSM; in the regions this figure is very low.
l.4: PM2.5 is a model estimate, not a measurement; climate is for the area's centre point.
l.5: In Karabakh and East Zangezur, population and infrastructure are changing fast, so the data may lag behind.
l.6: There is no congestion or real travel time; this would come only through an official Yandex/Waze partnership (no scraping).

quality.metaDesc: AI accuracy, number grounding and data checks: open, repeatable tests.
quality.intro: We compare how accurate the AI is against a simple rule-based approach, check that no numbers are invented and test the data itself. The tests are open and can be rerun. Last updated: {date} (Baku time).
quality.sampleNote: Sample sizes are small (10–30 cases); results are indicative only.
quality.intentBody: {n} queries in Azerbaijani (3 ambiguous, 2 misspelt or colloquial). Accuracy by field.
quality.intentEnBody: {n} queries in English (same schema, same checks).
quality.legalBody: {n} listing texts: 6 clean, 12 risky (including a hidden risk: “sənədlər sonra düzələcək”, documents to be sorted later).
quality.recall: Recall (how many risky listings were found)
quality.combined: On the site the two work together: any phrase the rule finds is always added to the AI's list, so known phrases are never missed.
quality.groundBody: Every number in {n} AI texts was extracted and looked up (±1%) in the JSON given to the model.
quality.groundEn: English profiles: {n} texts, {numbers} numbers, {pct}% found in the JSON.
quality.failH: 6. Our mistakes and how we fixed them
quality.cmpBody: The same task (“pick 3 areas in Nərimanov near the metro with a school and find their prices”): by hand with bina.az + Google Maps vs Məskən.
quality.cmpNote: User testing is under way; results and quotes will be added here. We make no claims until we have the numbers.

quality.poiH: 9. Services: OSM vs the official list
quality.poiBody: OSM counts for Baku's districts, Sumqayıt and Abşeron ({areas} areas) are compared with the opendata.az list (Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources). The sources are not added together. {checking} places have the status “Checking”; {custom} CUSTOMIZABLE_POINT entries are ignored.
quality.poiNote: OSM categories are broader (e.g. grocery kiosks, small green spaces) and the official list may be incomplete. A gap does not show which source is right; it shows where checking is needed.

official.metroNote: Source: Baku Metro (opendata.az). A trip is a turnstile entry; it shows how busy a station is, not how many people live nearby.
official.railFromCentre: from the area's centre, straight line
official.railNoise: Railway line {m} m away — possible noise
official.poiNote: Official list: Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources (opendata.az). The two sources are not added together; a gap shows where mapping is incomplete.
official.roadsNote: Source: State Statistics Committee. Public roads of national and local importance only; streets are excluded, so the figure is lower than the OSM length.
